Forme juridique de l'attributaire Le marché public sera conclu : – soit avec un opérateur économique unique ; 8/17 – soit avec un groupement d’opérateurs économiques conjoint ou solidaire. En cas de groupement conjoint, le mandataire sera solidaire, pour l'exécution du marché public, de chacun des membres du groupement, pour ses obligations contractuelles à l'égard de l’acheteur. La composition du groupement ne peut être modifiée entre la remise des offres et la date de signature du contrat. 2-6. ant indiquant qu'il ne tombe pas sous le coup d'une interdiction de soumissionner. Pour satisfaire aux obligations susmentionnées, le candidat qui envisage, dès le dépôt de son offre, de sous-traiter une partie de sa prestation, complètera utilement la déclaration de sous - traitance et joindra, pour chaque sous-traitant, l’ensemble des documents, attestations et renseignements réclamés aux candidats, tels que figurant au présent règlement de la consultation. La notification du marché public emporte acceptation du sous-traitant et agrément des conditions de paiement. Les prestations de services sont prouvées par des attestations du destinataire ou, à défaut, par une déclaration de l'opérateur économique ; • Une déclaration indiquant les effectifs moyens annuels du candidat et l'importance du personnel d'encadrement pendant les trois dernières années ; • Une description de l'outillage, du matériel et de l'équipement technique dont le candidat disposera pour la réalisation du marché public. Dans ce cas, il est également demandé de fournir dans le pli une copie de l’intégralité de la candidature et de l’offre sur support électronique (Clé USB, CD, DVD…). 6.1.5 - Signature des documents Le pouvoir adjudicateur a décidé d e privilégier une signature électronique pour la finalisation du contrat ! La signature électronique est exigée pour les pièces suivantes : - Lettre de candidature (DC1) ; - Acte d’engagement (AE). Les pièces transmises et pour lesquelles une signature est exigée peuvent être revêtues de la signature électronique sécurisée dès le dépôt de l’offre , en utilisant un certificat de signature électronique. Ce certificat doit être délivré par une autorité de certification accréditée et permettre de faire le lien entre une personne physique et le document signé électroniquement. Les candidats, qui auront choisi de ne pas signer les pièces de l’offre (pour lesquelles une signature est exigée) lors de leur dépôt, sont informés que l’attribution du marché donnera systématiquement lieu à la signature électronique de ces dernières. references_experience.text: (MVVM) development pattern, where you would have to code the presentation layer by creating View Models and Views for each object you wish to display, using NOF there is only a set of default generic (MVVM) views defined by NOF and they are applied to all domain objects (models). The Naked Objects pattern was first described formally in Richard Pawson's PhD thesis which includes a thorough investigation of various antecedents and inspirations for the pattern including, for example, the Morphic user interface. Naked Objects is commonly contrasted with the model-view-controller pattern. However, the published version of Pawson's thesis (see References) contains a foreword by Trygve Reenskaug, who first formulated the model-view-controller pattern, suggesting that Naked Objects is closer to the original intent of model-view-controller than many of the subsequent interpretations and implementations. Further information on the NO pattern is available at http://www.nakedobjects.org/ . Naked Objects 2.0 The BOMi currently uses version 2.0 of the Naked Objects framework, referred to as 'NOF2', which was the first publicly available framework to implement the 'naked objects pattern'. NOF2 was originally written by Naked Objects Group and supplied to the Department under an open-source licence.

Fixture scripts can also be used within the running application, facilitating manual/exploratory testing (discussed below). The Department also provides a number of other libraries to manage fixtures. The simple “fake data” library can be used in unit and other tests to select/generate a random value for use within a test. Integration tests should not hard-code any officer user Ids, instead the “officer leasing” library allows an unused user/officer account to be exclusively used, with logic to automatically check/reset the officer’s certificates for signed recorded actions. Production code should never use system time directly, instead it should be possible to “mock the clock” in tests. For the BOMi application the “Programmable Clock” service provides this capability. Keeping Tests Green Whenever a project starts the Department will ensure that the initial CI pipeline for their project branch (of the Trunk) is green. B2B: The DSP API and Electronic Exchange of Social Security Information (EESSI) APIs enable business-to-business integration to other Departments, public service bodies and to other European countries. Other supporting systems that make up the technology landscape include Facial Imaging Matching System (FIMS), and the General Registers Office (GRO) system. The BOMi’s scope will continue to grow in both size and complexity to (a) support the Department’s expanding Digital requirements, (b) consolidate its technology stack, and (c) continue to support new or changing legislation as it arises. The current technology platform is .NET Framework 4.x deployed to Windows Servers. In due course these will be upgraded to .NET 6 (aka .NET Core) at which time the Department will plan to deploy these systems, either for testing and/or production, on Linux/Docker when appropriate. New systems also target .NET 6 for the same purpose. The Department’s development resources are a combination of the Department’s internal staff, partnering with a number of service providers. The Senior Technical Development Advisor (TDA Lot 1) has acted as an independent strategic technical advisor across the IS Division, providing guidance on a range of SDLC and architecture related concerns. The TDA (Lot 1) helped product and platform teams deliver secure, resilient, and high-quality solutions more rapidly through the adoption of modern engineering practices and automation technologies. The TDA (Lot 1) role focused on shaping governance process and technical direction and procurement activities, translating complex technical issues into clear recommendations and implementation plans. Key areas of contribution included Continuous Integration, Release and Deployment, SDLC platform engineering, application security process and governance, Test Data Management modernisation, Developer Experience, contract testing, and SDLC platform architecture, particularly for the Department’s BOMi Platform. The TDA (Lot 1) also played a significant role in defining product and platform ownership models, associated team charters and enhanced IT governance approaches. In addition, the role supported various technical procurements through technical assessments.

Deshalb werden Angebote, bei denen der Bieter die Einheitspreise einzelner Leistungspositionen in „Mischkalkulationen“ auf andere Leistungspositionen umlegt, von der Wertung ausgeschlossen. De inschrijver is verplicht voor elk daarvan een volledig bod in te dienen. Het ontbreken van een van beide maakt het bod onvolledig. De gemeente behoudt zich het recht voor de opdracht te gunnen aan de oplossing van haar keuze op basis van de algemene prijs-kwaliteitsanalyse. Opties Vrije opties worden niet toegelaten. Our strategy sets a clear pathway to achieve net zero emissions in a way that supports our customers and ensures ESB’s continued growth. ESB are committed to leading the transition to a reliable and affordable net zero future. ESB seeks to purchase supplies, services and works that are produced or delivered in a manner that has the most positive environmental, social and economic impacts possible over their entire lifecycle. ESB procurement processes will be aligned with the standards from ISO20400, Sustainable Procurement. ESB have created a Sustainability Leadership Plan which sets out our ambitions and the actions we will take as they relate to the three pillars of sustainability - People, Planet and Place. Full details of ESB’s Sustainability Leadership Plan can be viewed here: ESB Sustainable Leadership Plan. ESB requires that the successful Contractor emerging from the Procurement process be familiar with our Sustainable Leadership Plan. Käsikirjadega saab tutvuda Google Drive kaustast Täpsem ajakava lepitakse eduka pakkujaga ühe kuu jooksul alates lepingu sõlmimisest. Pakkuja ja tellija lepivad kokku kooskõlastusringide tähtaegadest, vastutajatest ja kontaktisikutest. Ajakava koostamisel lähtutakse alljärgnevatest punktidest 5.3-5.11. Pakkuja töö hõlmab vähemalt järgmisi kooskõlastatud tööetappe: käsikirjade terviklik ülevaatus ja toimetamisvajaduse kaardistamine; ühe kooliastme klasside terminoloogia, struktuuri ja vormistuslahenduste ühtlustamine; kujunduskontseptsiooni ja näidiskülgede koostamine ning kooskõlastamine tellija ja autoritega; illustratsioonide, fotode, ikoonide ja muude visuaalsete elementide loomine või hankimine; esmane küljendus; katsetamise ja retsenseerimise tagasiside alusel muudatuste tegemine; lõplik keeleline ja tehniline korrektuur; trükifailide ettevalmistamine ja tellijapoolne kinnitamine enne trükki. Osades 1–3 kirjeldatud lõplike materjalide trükkimise eel viiakse läbi õppekomplektide katsetamine, milleks on vaja ette valmistada ja trükkida katsetuseksemplarid ja saata need katsetajatele. The Sizing Technology Pilot is a direct extension of this modernization mandate, seeking to apply advanced digital, computer vision, and AI-driven measurement extraction capabilities to a fundamental logistical process: Soldier and Cadet outfitting. The Army is exploring a Sizing Technology Pilot to modernize the Soldier and Cadet outfitting process by using body scanning, foot scanning, computer vision, and/or AI- driven measurement extraction to generate accurate measurements and translate them into recommended uniform and footwear sizing. This capability is intended to support personnel earlier in the accessions pipeline than is possible today, in support of a faster, more consistent, and more accurate issue experience. The scope of this requirement encompasses both body and foot scanning to modernize the issuance of both uniforms and footwear. forms_signatures.text: ment of the Army (HQDA) G-4 Logistics Initiatives Group is the directorate responsible for leading the Army’s digital transformation in logistics and Installation, Energy, and Environment (IE&E). The G-4 drives policy, governance, investment strategy, and the technical integration of logistics automated information management systems. Their strategic focus centers on logistics modernization through integrated information systems, scaling artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) analytics, and improving supply chain reliability across Army operations. The Sizing Technology Pilot is a direct extension of this modernization mandate, seeking to apply advanced digital, computer vision, and AI-driven measurement extraction capabilities to a fundamental logistical process: Soldier and Cadet outfitting. The Army is exploring a Sizing Technology Pilot to modernize the Soldier and Cadet outfitting process by using body scanning, foot scanning, computer vision, and/or AI- driven measurement extraction to generate accurate measurements and translate them into recommended uniform and footwear sizing. This capability is intended to support personnel earlier in the accessions pipeline than is possible today, in support of a faster, more consistent, and more accurate iss

l, non- contact methods and translating those measurements into recommended standard Army uniform and footwear sizes. Accurate measurement-to-size mapping — not a 3D visual try-on or avatar rendering, is the core capability sought. The Army is seeking a solution that will operate reliably across a wide spectrum of Army operating environments, minimize the training burden on Soldiers and administering staff, and be capable of integrating with designated Army data systems to support downstream sizing and issue processes. 3. REQUIRED AND DESIRED SOLUTION ATTRIBUTES. Required Attributes: The proposed solution shall meet the following mandatory requirements: • Comprehensive Scanning and Environmental Resilience: Must capture both body and foot measurements sufficient to determine standard Army uniform and footwear sizing using automated, digital, non-contact methods that eliminate manual measurements. The capture hardware must be transportable and capable of operating reliably across a wide spectrum of environments, including indoor facilities and austere outdoor settings, accommodating real-world conditions such as variable ambient lighting and physical space constraints. • Data Translation & Mapping: Must translate captured body and foot measurements into recommen

tive, requiring minimal training for both the Soldiers and Cadets being measured and the administering staff. • Security & Compliance: Must comply with all applicable DoD Risk Management Framework (RMF) requirements and be capable of obtaining the appropriate Authorization to Operate (ATO) prior to processing any Soldier and Cadet data (all captured data must be encrypted at rest and in transit). Impact Level 5 (IL5) is required prior to full-scale enterprise deployment. Pilot execution will be conducted in an isolated, test/dummy network environment. • Data Management & Privacy: Must support a defined data retention and deletion schedule that strictly adheres to Army records-management and Privacy Act requirements. • Inclusive Accuracy: Must produce accurate measurements across the complete spectrum of body types, statures, and physical compositions represented in the Army accession and training population. • Accessibility (Section 508): Must provide an accessible alternative process for Soldiers and Cadets who are unable to use, or elect not to use, the scanning solution; any user-facing digital interface must strictly comply with Section 508 accessibility standards. • Data Ownership & Licensing: Must allow the Government to retain exclusive ownership of all Soldier and Cadet sizing data as well as any vendor-generated technical or derived data. • Hardware Agility & Openness: The proposed solution must be hardware- agnostic to the greatest extent possible, avoiding dependency on proprietary, single-source capture devices. The software application must be capable of evolving to support new generations of commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) devices. The physical hardware proposed for the pilot must be agile, deployable, and suitable for the respective operating environments

There is no minimum TRL level for a Phase 1 innovation to advance to Phase 2. Small businesses must still meet the Eligibility Criteria in 1.4 and must provide all documentation outlined in Attachment 3 when requested. A request for documentation does not guarantee that a Phase 2 contract will be awarded. Small businesses should not have any expectations of being invited to advance to Phase 2.
